title: Spoken article
description: A cobalt reading card follows a short essay sentence by sentence using the browser’s own voice.
useCase: Offer a spoken version of editorial content with visible position and intentional playback.
interaction: Listen, pause, select a sentence or change the speaking rate.
reducedMotion: Sentence state changes are immediate; speech plays only after an explicit request.
limitations: Available voices and boundary events vary by browser and device. Resume uses the last reported word boundary; speech is not a rendered audio asset.
look: Near-white page in cobalt blue: italic serif headline, three serif sentences, a solid cobalt play button, a thin segmented progress line and rate label.
motion: Pressing play speaks the article with the browser's speech synthesis; the spoken sentence gets a pale blue highlight and underline, and a three-segment progress line fills, both switching instantly.
adapt: Playback is `speak`, which creates one `SpeechSynthesisUtterance` per sentence, records `onboundary` offsets for resume and advances on `onend`; the highlight is `.sa-copy button[aria-current=true]`. Replace `SENTENCES` and the headline; the rate cycle sits in the `sa-rate` handler.
